subject.title: [Feature Request]: Session snapshots — save and load context checkpoints (/session save|load)

question: Should OpenClaw own first-class named session snapshots, and what initial semantics should cover named save/load, branch/restore, archive import, and prompt-cache-aware forks?
rationale: The request crosses durable storage, session lifecycle, Gateway protocol, slash/CLI/UI UX, destructive restore semantics, archive privacy/retention, and prompt-cache behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/API contract.

options.title: Design core snapshot contract first
options.body: Specify named save/list/load/branch semantics, canonical storage, retention, security, archive import behavior, and migration boundaries before implementation.

options.title: Ship a narrower resume slice first
options.body: Limit near-term work to safe session listing/resume or read-only family-history recovery while leaving arbitrary named snapshots and templates for a later design.

options.title: Keep adjacent primitives only
options.body: Decline first-class named snapshots and continue tracking compaction checkpoints, archive recovery, and fork/resume as separate narrower issues.

recommendation.title: Design core snapshot contract first
recommendation.body: Specify named save/list/load/branch semantics, canonical storage, retention, security, archive import behavior, and migration boundaries before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved blocker is product/API semantics across multiple session surfaces rather than a single-file implementation detail.
